In [[multilinear algebra]], applying a map that is the [[Tensor product#Tensor product of linear maps|tensor product of linear maps]] to a [[tensor]] is called a '''multilinear multiplication'''.

== Abstract definition ==
Let <math>F
   </math> be a field of characteristic zero, such as <math>\mathbb{R}
   </math> or <math>\mathbb{C}
   </math>.
Let <math>V_k</math> be a finite-dimensional vector space over <math>F</math>, and let <math>\mathcal{A} \in V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes V_d</math> be an order-d simple [[tensor]], i.e., there exist some vectors <math>\mathbf{v}_k \in V_k</math> such that <math>\mathcal{A} = \mathbf{v}_1 \otimes \mathbf{v}_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{v}_d</math>. If we are given a collection of linear maps <math>A_k : V_k \to W_k</math>, then the '''multilinear multiplication''' of <math>\mathcal{A}</math> with <math>(A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_d)</math> is defined<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Tensors : geometry and applications|last=M.|first=Landsberg, J.|date=2012|publisher=American Mathematical Society|isbn=9780821869079|location=Providence, R.I.|oclc=733546583}}</ref> as the action on <math>\mathcal{A}</math> of the [[tensor product]] of these linear maps,<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9780387902845|title=Multilinear Algebra {{!}} Werner Greub {{!}} Springer|series=Universitext|year=1978|publisher=Springer|isbn=9780387902845|language=en}}</ref> namely

<math display="block">
\begin{align}
A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d : V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes V_d & \to W_1 \otimes W_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes W_d, \\
\mathbf{v}_1 \otimes \mathbf{v}_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{v}_d & \mapsto A_1(\mathbf{v}_1) \otimes A_2(\mathbf{v}_2) \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d(\mathbf{v}_d)
\end{align}
</math>

Since the [[tensor product]] of linear maps is itself a linear map,<ref name=":1" /> and because every tensor admits a [[tensor rank decomposition]],<ref name=":0" /> the above expression extends linearly to all tensors. That is, for a general tensor <math>\mathcal{A} \in V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes V_d</math>, the multilinear multiplication is

<math display="block">
\begin{align}
& \mathcal{B} := (A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d)(\mathcal{A}) \\[4pt]
= {} & (A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d)\left(\sum_{i=1}^r \mathbf{a}_i^1 \otimes \mathbf{a}_i^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{a}_i^d\right) \\[5pt]
= {} & \sum_{i=1}^r A_1(\mathbf{a}_i^1) \otimes A_2(\mathbf{a}_i^2) \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d( \mathbf{a}_i^d )
\end{align}
</math>

where <math display="inline">\mathcal{A} = \sum_{i=1}^r \mathbf{a}_i^1 \otimes \mathbf{a}_i^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{a}_i^d</math> with <math>\mathbf{a}_i^k \in V_k</math> is one of <math>\mathcal{A}</math>'s tensor rank decompositions. The validity of the above expression is not limited to a tensor rank decomposition; in fact, it is valid for any expression of <math>\mathcal{A}</math> as a [[linear combination]] of pure tensors, which follows from the [[Tensor product#Universal property|universal property of the tensor product]].

It is standard to use the following shorthand notations in the literature for multilinear multiplications:<math display="block">
(A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_d) \cdot \mathcal{A} := (A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d)(\mathcal{A}) 
</math>and<math display="block">
A_k \cdot_k \mathcal{A} := (\operatorname{Id}_{V_1}, \ldots, \operatorname{Id}_{V_{k-1}}, A_k, \operatorname{Id}_{V_{k+1}}, \ldots, \operatorname{Id}_{V_{d}}) \cdot \mathcal{A},
</math>where <math>\operatorname{Id}_{V_k} : V_k \to V_k </math> is the [[identity operator]].

== Definition in coordinates ==
In computational multilinear algebra it is conventional to work in coordinates. Assume that an [[Inner product space|inner product]] is fixed on <math>V_k</math> and let <math>V_k^*</math> denote the [[dual vector space]] of <math>V_k </math>. Let <math>\{ e_1^k, \ldots, e_{n_k}^k \} </math> be a basis for <math>V_k </math>, let <math>\{ (e_1^k)^*, \ldots, (e_{n_k}^k)^* \} </math> be the dual basis, and let <math>\{f_1^k, \ldots, f_{m_k}^k \} </math> be a basis for <math>W_k </math>. The linear map <math display="inline">M_k = \sum_{i=1}^{m_k} \sum_{j=1}^{n_k} m_{i,j}^{(k)} f_i^k \otimes (e_j^k)^* </math> is then represented by the matrix <math>\widehat{M}_k = [m_{i,j}^{(k)}] \in F^{m_k \times n_k}</math>.  Likewise, with respect to the standard tensor product basis <math>\{ e_{j_1}^1 \otimes e_{j_2}^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes e_{j_d}^d \}_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d}  </math>, the abstract tensor<math display="block">\mathcal{A} = \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} e_{j_1}^1 \otimes e_{j_2}^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes e_{j_d}^d
   </math>is represented by the multidimensional array <math>\widehat{\mathcal{A}} = [a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d}] \in F^{n_1 \times n_2 \times \cdots \times n_d}
   </math> . Observe that <math display="block">\widehat{\mathcal{A}} = \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1 \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_2}^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d,
   </math>

where <math>\mathbf{e}_j^k \in F^{n_k} </math> is the ''j''th [[standard basis]] vector of <math>F^{n_k} </math> and the tensor product of vectors is the affine [[Segre map]] <math>\otimes : (\mathbf{v}^{(1)}, \mathbf{v}^{(2)}, \ldots, \mathbf{v}^{(d)}) \mapsto [v_{i_1}^{(1)} v_{i_2}^{(2)} \cdots v_{i_d}^{(d)}]_{i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_d} </math>. It follows from the above choices of bases that the multilinear multiplication <math>\mathcal{B} = (M_1, M_2, \ldots, M_d) \cdot \mathcal{A}</math> becomes

<math display="block" id="abba">
\begin{align}
\widehat{\mathcal{B}} &= (\widehat{M}_1, \widehat{M}_2, \ldots, \widehat{M}_d) \cdot \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1 \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_2}^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d \\
&= \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} (\widehat{M}_1, \widehat{M}_2, \ldots, \widehat{M}_d) \cdot (\mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1 \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_2}^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d) \\
&= \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} (\widehat{M}_1 \mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1) \otimes (\widehat{M}_2 \mathbf{e}_{j_2}^2) \otimes \cdots \otimes (\widehat{M}_d \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d).
\end{align}
</math>

The resulting tensor <math>\widehat{\mathcal{B}}</math> lives in <math>F^{m_1 \times m_2 \times \cdots \times m_d}</math>.

=== Element-wise definition ===
From the above expression, an element-wise definition of the multilinear multiplication is obtained. Indeed, since <math>\widehat{\mathcal{B}}</math> is a multidimensional array, it may be expressed as <math display="block">\widehat{\mathcal{B}} = \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} b_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1 \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_2}^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d,
   </math>where <math>b_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \in F
   </math> are the coefficients. Then it follows from the above formulae that

<math display="block">
\begin{align}
& \left( (\mathbf{e}_{i_1}^1)^T, (\mathbf{e}_{i_2}^2)^T, \ldots, (\mathbf{e}_{i_d}^d)^T \right) \cdot \widehat{\mathcal{B}} \\
= {} & \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} b_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \left( (\mathbf{e}_{i_1}^1)^T \mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1 \right) \otimes \left((\mathbf{e}_{i_2}^2)^T \mathbf{e}_{j_2}^2\right) \otimes \cdots \otimes \left( (\mathbf{e}_{i_d}^d)^T \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d \right) \\
= {} & \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} b_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \delta_{i_1, j_1} \cdot \delta_{i_2,j_2} \cdots \delta_{i_d, j_d} \\
= {} & b_{i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_d},
\end{align}
</math>

where <math>\delta_{i,j} </math> is the [[Kronecker delta]]. Hence, if <math>\mathcal{B} = (M_1, M_2, \ldots, M_d) \cdot \mathcal{A} </math>, then

<math display="block" >
\begin{align}
& b_{i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_d} = \left( (\mathbf{e}_{i_1}^1)^T, (\mathbf{e}_{i_2}^2)^T, \ldots, (\mathbf{e}_{i_d}^d)^T \right) \cdot \widehat{\mathcal{B}} \\
= {} & \left( (\mathbf{e}_{i_1}^1)^T, (\mathbf{e}_{i_2}^2)^T, \ldots, (\mathbf{e}_{i_d}^d)^T \right) \cdot (\widehat{M}_1, \widehat{M}_2, \ldots, \widehat{M}_d) \cdot 
\sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1 \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_2}^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d \\
= {} & \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} ((\mathbf{e}_{i_1}^1)^T \widehat{M}_1 \mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1) \otimes ((\mathbf{e}_{i_2}^2)^T \widehat{M}_2 \mathbf{e}_{j_2}^2) \otimes \cdots \otimes ((\mathbf{e}_{i_d}^d)^T \widehat{M}_d \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d) \\
= {} & \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} m_{i_1,j_1}^{(1)} \cdot m_{i_2,j_2}^{(2)} \cdots m_{i_d,j_d}^{(d)},
\end{align}
</math>

where the <math>m_{i,j}^{(k)} </math> are the elements of <math>\widehat{M}_k </math> as defined above.

== Properties ==
Let <math>\mathcal{A} \in V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes V_d </math> be an order-d tensor over the tensor product of <math>F </math>-vector spaces.  

Since a multilinear multiplication is the tensor product of linear maps, we have the following multilinearity property (in the construction of the map):<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

<math display="block">A_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_{k-1} \otimes (\alpha A_k + \beta B) \otimes A_{k+1} \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d = 
\alpha A_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d + \beta A_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_{k-1} \otimes B \otimes A_{k+1} \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d 
</math> 

Multilinear multiplication is a [[linear map]]:<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> <math display="block">(M_1, M_2, \ldots, M_d) \cdot (\alpha \mathcal{A} + \beta \mathcal{B}) 
= \alpha \; (M_1, M_2, \ldots, M_d) \cdot \mathcal{A} +
\beta \; (M_1, M_2, \ldots, M_d) \cdot \mathcal{B} </math> 

It follows from the definition that the [[Composition of maps|composition]] of two multilinear multiplications is also a multilinear multiplication:<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

<math display="block">(M_1, M_2, \ldots, M_d) \cdot \left( (K_1, K_2, \ldots, K_d) \cdot \mathcal{A} \right)
= (M_1 \circ K_1, M_2 \circ K_2, \ldots, M_d \circ K_d) \cdot \mathcal{A}, </math>

where <math>M_k : U_k \to W_k</math> and <math>K_k : V_k \to U_k</math> are linear maps.

Observe specifically that multilinear multiplications in different factors commute,

<math display="block">M_k \cdot_k \left( M_\ell \cdot_\ell \mathcal{A} \right) 
= M_\ell \cdot_\ell \left( M_k \cdot_k \mathcal{A} \right) 
= M_k \cdot_k M_\ell \cdot_\ell \mathcal{A}, 
</math>

if <math>k \ne \ell.</math>

== Computation ==
The factor-k multilinear multiplication <math>M_k \cdot_k\mathcal{A}</math> can be computed in coordinates as follows. Observe first that

<math display="block">
\begin{align}
M_k \cdot_k \mathcal{A} &= M_k \cdot_k 
\sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \sum_{j_2=1}^{n_2} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1 \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_2}^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d \\
&= \sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \cdots \sum_{j_{k-1}=1}^{n_{k-1}} \sum_{j_{k+1}=1}^{n_{k+1}} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} \mathbf{e}_{j_1}^1 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_{k-1}}^{k-1} \otimes M_k \left ( \sum_{j_k=1}^{n_k} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \mathbf{e}_{j_k}^k \right) \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_{k+1}}^{k+1} \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathbf{e}_{j_d}^d.
\end{align}
</math>

Next, since

<math display="block">F^{n_1} \otimes F^{n_2} \otimes \cdots \otimes F^{n_d} 
\simeq F^{n_k} \otimes (F^{n_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes F^{n_{k-1}} \otimes F^{n_{k+1}} \otimes \cdots \otimes F^{n_d}) 
\simeq F^{n_k} \otimes F^{n_1 \cdots n_{k-1} n_{k+1} \cdots n_d},
</math>

there is a bijective map, called the '''factor-''k'' standard [[Tensor reshaping|flattening]]''',<ref name=":0" /> denoted by <math>(\cdot)_{(k)} </math>, that identifies <math>M_k \cdot_k \mathcal{A}</math> with an element from the latter space, namely

<math display="block">\left( M_k \cdot_k \mathcal{A} \right)_{(k)} :=
\sum_{j_1=1}^{n_1} \cdots \sum_{j_{k-1}=1}^{n_{k-1}} \sum_{j_{k+1}=1}^{n_{k+1}} \cdots \sum_{j_d=1}^{n_d} M_k \left ( \sum_{j_k=1}^{n_k} a_{j_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d} \mathbf{e}_{j_{k}}^{k} \right) \otimes \mathbf{e}_{\mu_k(j_1,\ldots,j_{k-1},j_{k+1},\ldots,j_d)} := M_k \mathcal{A}_{(k)}, 
   </math>

where <math>\mathbf{e}_j </math>is the ''j''th standard basis vector of <math>F^{N_k}</math>, <math>N_k = n_1 \cdots n_{k-1} n_{k+1} \cdots n_d </math>, and <math>\mathcal{A}_{(k)} \in F^{n_k} \otimes F^{N_k} \simeq F^{n_k \times N_k} </math> is the '''factor-''k'' flattening matrix''' of <math>\mathcal{A}</math> whose columns are the '''factor-''k'' vectors''' <math>[a_{j_1,\ldots,j_{k-1},i,j_{k+1},\ldots,j_d}]_{i=1}^{n_k} </math> in some order, determined by the particular choice of the bijective map

<math display="block">\mu_k : [1,n_1] \times \cdots \times [1,n_{k-1}] \times [1,n_{k+1}] \times \cdots \times [1,n_d] \to [1,N_k]. 
</math>

In other words, the multilinear multiplication <math>(M_1, M_2, \ldots, M_d) \cdot \mathcal{A}</math> can be computed as a sequence of ''d'' factor-''k'' multilinear multiplications, which themselves can be implemented efficiently as classic matrix multiplications.

== Applications ==
The [[higher-order singular value decomposition]] (HOSVD) factorizes a tensor given in coordinates <math>\mathcal{A} \in F^{n_1 \times n_2 \times \cdots \times n_d} </math> as the multilinear multiplication <math>\mathcal{A} = (U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_d) \cdot \mathcal{S} </math>, where <math>U_k \in F^{n_k \times n_k} </math> are [[Orthogonal matrix|orthogonal matrices]] and <math>\mathcal{S} \in F^{n_1 \times n_2 \times \cdots \times n_d} </math>.
